title: Quogue Historical Society — Shinnecock Family History
summary: A public museum and research collection preserving Quogue history, including the Enos family and the Shinnecock Arms.
address_label: Pond House, 114 Jessup Avenue, Quogue, NY 11959
map_geometry_source: OpenStreetMap way 466654634 and address node 8791904819, Quogue Historical Society Museum; cross-checked with the official 114 Jessup Avenue address, September 18, 2026.
why_this_matters: Read alongside family records, the 1938 Shinnecock Arms listing shows how local history reaches beyond buildings and place names into work, hospitality and the barriers travelers faced. Keeping these records accessible makes those relationships part of Quogue’s public history.
introduction_title: Native family history beyond the place name
introduction_content: The Quogue Historical Society preserves evidence of Shinnecock family life within the village. Its research draws on a 1992 oral history by descendant Muriel Barnes Rains and documents relating to the Enos family and Shinnecock Arms. The Enos family and Shinnecock Arms, Quogue
history_title: The Enos family, work and hospitality
history_content:
Abram Edwin Enos built the family home in 1899. His wife, Mary Nancy Lee Enos, was Shinnecock. Their daughter, schoolteacher Mathilda “Tillie” Enos Dent, later operated it as the Shinnecock Arms, accommodating workers employed by summer residents. The Enos family and Shinnecock Arms, Quogue

The 1938 Negro Motorist Green Book lists Shinnecock Arms under Quogue’s summer resorts. The entry places this family history within the wider network of lodgings available to Black travelers during segregation. The Negro Motorist Green Book, 1938, p. 21

The Society moved into Pond House in 2011. The museum pin identifies this public research and interpretation site; the family’s former home and boarding house were at a separate location. Quogue Historical Society — Our History
whereintheworld_content: Pond House is at 114 Jessup Avenue, Quogue. Check museum hours and appointment information before visiting. This pin does not identify the Enos residence or imply that a family-history exhibit is currently on view. Quogue Historical Society — Hours and Location
